deep.reconstruction:
This is printed p. 21 of Riemann's 1857 paper 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 7). It is not an unpublished manuscript; the running head and page number show it is the offprint. Throughout, the Riemann condition α+α'+β+β'+γ+γ'=1 holds.

(A) End of Art. VII (continued from p. 20).
- The integral I(x) = x^α (1-x)^γ ∫ s^{-α'-β'-γ'} (1-s)^{-α'-β-γ} (1-xs)^{-α-β'-γ} ds is taken between any two of the four points 0, 1, 1/x, ∞ along any path.
- Riemann asserts that I(x) is a branch of P{α β γ; α' β' γ'; x}. With a suitable choice of endpoints and path it gives each of the six special branches P^α, P^α', P^β, P^β', P^γ, P^γ'.
- Riemann obtained it by inserting Euler integrals for the Π-functions in the series of p. 20 and interchanging sum and integral.
- Worked check (mine): take endpoints 0 and 1. Using the Riemann condition, -α'-β'-γ' = α+β+γ-1. Set b = α+β+γ, a = α+β'+γ, c = 1+α-α'. Then c-b-1 = -α'-β-γ, and the integrand is s^{b-1}(1-s)^{c-b-1}(1-xs)^{-a}. Euler's integral then gives I = B(b,c-b) · x^α (1-x)^γ · F(a,b;c;x), which is the P^α branch.
- He promises a later direct proof that I has the defining properties of a P-function. This integral will later be used to fix the still-arbitrary constant factors of P^α, P^α', ….
- He remarks that the path must be modified when the integrand is non-integrable at one of the endpoints 0, 1, 1/x, ∞. This is the problem later solved by loop/double-loop (Pochhammer-type) contours.

(B) Art. VIII, first step: series expansion of P^α.
- From Art. II (the exponent shift x^λ(1-x)^μ P = P with shifted exponents) and Art. VII:
  P^α{α β γ; α' β' γ'; x} = x^α (1-x)^γ P^α{0, β+α+γ, 0; α'-α, β'+α+γ, γ'-γ; x} = Const · x^α (1-x)^γ F(α+β+γ, α+β'+γ, 1+α-α', x).
- Check (mine): the shifted exponents sum to (α'-α)+(β+α+γ)+(β'+α+γ)+(γ'-γ) = 1, as required.
- Comparison with F(a,b,c,x) = P(0, a, 0; 1-c, b, c-a-b; x) from p. 20 gives a = α+β+γ, b = α+β'+γ, c = 1+α-α'.
- Then c-a-b = 1-α-α'-β-β'-2γ = γ'-γ, again using the Riemann condition. So the identification is consistent.

(C) Art. VIII, counting the expansions.
- By Art. V, any function has 8 P-representations with the same variable x. These come from the 2^3 interchanges α↔α', β↔β', γ↔γ'.
- The interchange β↔β' gives the same series, since F is symmetric in a and b. So there are 4 distinct expansions in rising powers of x.
- Two of them, related by γ↔γ', represent P^α:
  x^α (1-x)^γ F(α+β+γ, α+β'+γ, 1+α-α', x) and x^α (1-x)^γ' F(α+β+γ', α+β'+γ', 1+α-α', x).
  These are equal by Euler's transformation F(a,b;c;x) = (1-x)^{c-a-b} F(c-a, c-b; c; x). Here c-a = α+β+γ' and c-b = α+β'+γ', using the Riemann condition.
- The other two represent P^α'.
- All four converge for |x|<1 and diverge for |x|>1. The page breaks off saying the series in falling powers of x (representing P^β, P^β') behave conversely.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every exponent identity checks under α+α'+β+β'+γ+γ'=1.

The claim that a suitable choice of endpoints and path yields every one of the six branches is stated without proof here. Proof is deferred ('in der Folge'), and for degenerate exponents a path modification is needed, which Riemann himself notes.

results.what: Euler-type integral representation of a general Riemann P-function: x^α(1-x)^γ ∫ s^{-α'-β'-γ'}(1-s)^{-α'-β-γ}(1-xs)^{-α-β'-γ} ds between two of the points 0, 1, 1/x, ∞ gives the branches P^α, …, P^γ'.
results.modern_name: Euler integral representation of hypergeometric / Riemann P-functions (Euler-type integrals between singular points)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (integral for F); the general P-function form is credited to Riemann 1857

results.what: Remark that the integration path must be modified when the integrand is non-integrable at an endpoint.
results.modern_name: Loop / Pochhammer double-loop contours (regularisation of Euler integrals)
results.usually_credited_to: Pochhammer 1890 (Jordan, Hankel for related loop integrals); Riemann's remark is known

results.what: P^α = Const · x^α (1-x)^γ F(α+β+γ, α+β'+γ, 1+α-α', x) via the exponent-shift rule.
results.modern_name: Local Frobenius solution at x=0 of the Riemann (Papperitz) equation in terms of 2F1

results.what: Counting: 8 P-representations per variable give 4 distinct series in powers of x (2 for P^α, 2 for P^α', related by Euler's transformation); this builds toward the 24 series.
results.modern_name: Kummer's 24 solutions of the hypergeometric equation; Euler transformation
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer 1836 (24 solutions), Euler (transformation); Riemann's P-symbol derivation of 1857
